name: CheckSettingMode

note: test mode start: clears system mode, RAM and both palette banks, sets up the BIOS RAM, then TestMenu

name: TestMenu

name: PutBcdByte

name: TestMenuText

name: PutWeekday
note: appends the 3-letter name of BIOS_WEEKDAY from WeekdayNames

name: WeekdayNames
note: SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT, 4 bytes each ($FF ends a name)

name: TestMenuSelect
note: pushes TestMenu as the return address and jumps to TestMenuJumpTable[WorkIndex]

note: 7 entries in menu order: HardwareTest, TestHardDip, TestSoftDip, TestBookKeeping, TestCodeNumber, TestCalendar, TestMenuExit

name: TestCalendar

name: HwTestStepTable
note: 14 entries: for each of the 7 screens a draw routine and a per-frame routine

name: HwTestCrosshatch

name: HwTestCrosshatchFrame

name: HwTestColorBars

note: per frame routine of the hardware-test calendar

name: WaitFrame
note: sets FrameWaitFlag and loops until SystemInt1 (VBlank) clears it

name: Reset
note: target of the reset vector and ENTRY_RESET

name: SystemInt1
note: target of SYSTEM_INT1 (VBlank routine called by games)

name: SystemInt2
note: target of SYSTEM_INT2, the level 2 (timer) handler of the system ROM vector table: acknowledges the timer IRQ and turns it off (LSPCMODE $4000). Safety net for HOW_TO_PLAY, the only BIOS call that maps the system ROM vectors and lowers the mask without writing LSPCMODE. MAME: ran when the timer IRQ was forced on inside HOW_TO_PLAY in NAM-1975; no checked game runs it on its own

name: SystemReturn
note: target of SYSTEM_RETURN

name: SystemIo
note: target of SYSTEM_IO

name: CreditCheck
note: target of CREDIT_CHECK: MVS, free play off (hard DIP 7, bit 6 of REG_DIPSW): BCD check of the requested credits ($10FDB0) against Credits

name: CreditDown
note: target of CREDIT_DOWN (wiki); MAME: King of the Monsters 2 calls it after CREDIT_CHECK when one player picks PLAYER1 PLAYER2 vs COMPUTER (credits 02 -> 01, the second player's credit)

name: ReadCalendar
note: target of READ_CALENDAR

name: SetupCalendar
note: target of SETUP_CALENDAR (wiki); MAME: runs when D is pressed on the test-mode calendar screen

name: Card
note: target of CARD: returns $80 (no card) when REG_STATUS_B bits 4-5 are set, else jumps through CardFunctionTable[BIOS_CRDF]

name: CardError
note: target of CARD_ERROR (wiki); MAME with a blank (unformatted) card: runs when the game starts, after CardDataSearch

name: HowToPlay
note: target of HOW_TO_PLAY (wiki); MAME: NAM-1975, Mahjong Kyoretsuden and Baseball Stars Professional call it after START (joystick and buttons animated, the game captions); none of the other 15 checked games references it

name: ChecksumLoop
note: target of the checksum slot at $C0047A (CHECKSUM_LOOP): adds every byte of the cartridge P ROM (CART_PROM_SIZE bytes, kicking the watchdog), subtracts the header byte $186, writes the result to $186 and WorkRamStart, then loops until the watchdog resets the system. Nothing calls the slot; ran in MAME from a test build (scenario checksum_loop: Sengoku 2, 1 MB summed in 207 frames, sum $EF, reset 8 frames later)

name: FixClear
note: target of FIX_CLEAR

name: LspFirst
note: target of LSP_1ST (clear sprites)

name: MessOut
note: target of MESS_OUT

name: ControllerSetup
note: target of CONTROLLER_SETUP

name: PowerOnTest
note: boot tests: LED latches, then work RAM, backup RAM, palette banks 1/0 and VRAM (test number in d6), calendar, system ROM checksum, memory card; errors go to BootError

name: WorkRamTestLoop
note: when REG_DIPSW reads 0 (all hard DIPs on): shows WORK RAM TEST and repeats the RAM tests until a DIP is turned off

name: BootErrorMemCard
note: d6 = 7 (MEMORY CARD ERROR), then BootError

name: BootErrorCalendar
note: d6 = 5 (CALENDAR ERROR) when VBlankCount between two calendar pulses is outside $39-$3F (57-63 frames, about 1 s), then BootError

name: WaitRtcPulse
note: waits for a rising edge of bit 6 of REG_STATUS_A (calendar pulse, wiki register page)

name: RtcCommand
note: sends the 4-bit command in d0 to the calendar chip, bit by bit through sub_C12DB0

name: MemTestBlock
note: memory test of d5+1 words from a0 (test number in d6), used for work RAM and palette banks

name: BackupRamTest
note: power-on test of backup RAM (test number in d6). Hard DIPs not all on: when BackupRamSignature equals BackupRamOkText, returns at once and the contents are kept; otherwise MemTestBlock on backup RAM, then ClearBackupRam. All hard DIPs on (REG_DIPSW = 0): MemTestBlock only, every time (WorkRamTestLoop). MAME: signature found on a second boot with the same nvram, ClearBackupRam on a first boot and on the boot after a NEO-CLN or NoGoIdText cartridge

name: ClearBackupRam
note: unlocks backup RAM, fills all 64 KB with zeros from $D10000 down, writes BackupRamSignature, copies BackupRamDefaults to $D0003A-$D00046, sets $D00122 = $23, SlotTable all $FFFF, $D001AC = $F0F0F0F0, $D001B0 = $FFFF, locks it. Book keeping and settings are lost

name: VramTest
note: VRAM test through REG_VRAMRW, d4 start address, d5 count

name: Delay
note: nested BSR chain into sub_C18500: a fixed delay used between LED latch writes

name: BootError
note: error screen: message BootErrorMessages[d6]; for d6 < 5 also prints the failing address and data

name: BootErrorMessages
note: pointers to the boot error texts: 0 WORK RAM, 1 BACKUP RAM, 2 COLOR RAM BANK0, 3 COLOR RAM BANK1, 4 VIDEO RAM, 5 CALENDAR, 6 SYSTEM ROM, 7 MEMORY CARD

name: ClearRamAndVideo
note: clears work RAM, both palette banks, the fix layer (FixClear), sprite VRAM, then LspFirst

name: BiosStart
note: after the tests: MESS_OUT buffer, ControllerSetup, then SystemModeDispatch

name: SystemModeDispatch
note: resets the stack, then jumps through SystemModeTable by the low byte of BIOS_SYSTEM_MODE

name: SystemModeTable
note: 3 entries: SystemMode0, SystemMode1, SystemMode2

name: SystemMode0
note: mode 0: selects the slot (SelectSlot), loads the game soft DIPs (LoadGameSoftDips), then CallUser with request 0 (init)

name: SystemMode1
note: mode 1, eyecatcher: CART_EYECATCH_FLAG 0 runs the system ROM Eyecatcher, 1 calls the game (CallUser request 1), 2 skips to mode 2

name: SystemMode2
note: mode 2: only when SlotNumberMode is set, shows SLOT n (SlotText, CurrentSlot + 1) for up to 300 frames, ended early by SELECT P1 (bit 1 of BIOS_STATCHANGE_RAW); then CallUser with request 2 (demo), or 3 (title) when Credits is non-zero and $D00043 is 0

name: Eyecatcher
note: system ROM eyecatcher (NEO-GEO logo, MAX 330 MEGA, SNK), reached when CART_EYECATCH_FLAG is 0; MAME boot sequence

name: ReadControllers
note: selects the joystick ports through REG_POUTPUT, reads REG_P1CNT/REG_P2CNT/REG_STATUS_B and updates BIOS_P1STATUS and the following input bytes

name: MvsLedUpdate
note: MVS only: credit LED / marquee latch handling at the start of SystemIo

name: PlayTimeCount
note: MVS, while a game runs (BIOS_USER_MODE 2): every 60 frames adds 1 to a long in backup RAM ($D00048, through a4 = $D08000)

name: CallUser
note: hands over to the game: BIOS_USER_REQUEST = d0, BIOS_SYSTEM_MODE = d1 | $80, cartridge vectors (REG_SWPROM), backup RAM locked, jmp CART_USER

name: SlotText
note: MESS_OUT text "SLOT " used by SystemMode2

name: LoadGameSoftDips
note: copies the current game soft DIP block from backup RAM into BIOS_GAME_DIP (6 bytes, then 12 nibbles)

name: SelectSlot
note: scans the slot table in backup RAM ($D00124, 4 bytes per slot) from the slot in $D00109

name: CheckPlayerStart
note: SystemIo while a game runs: start buttons from BIOS_STATCHANGE set BIOS_START_FLAG; on the title with credits the BCD BIOS_SELECT_TIMER counts down and forces a start; calls CART_PLAYER_START, then mode 3

name: StartCreditCheck
note: MVS: checks the requested starts in BIOS_START_FLAG against the credits before CART_PLAYER_START

name: CardFunctionTable
note: 8 entries indexed by BIOS_CRDF (wiki CARD: 0 format, 1 data search, 2 load, 3 save, 4 delete, 5 read data title, 6 save user name, 7 load user name)

name: CardFormat
note: CARD function 0: format memory card (wiki); MAME: runs when the card utility formats a card (test build)

name: CardDataSearch
note: CARD function 1: data search (wiki); MAME with a blank card: called when the game starts

name: CardLoadData
note: CARD function 2: load data (wiki); MAME: Sengoku 2 LOAD prompt with a saved card, the game resumes in its second area

name: CardSaveData
note: CARD function 3: save data (wiki); MAME: Sengoku 2 SAVE prompt after losing in level 2, writes SENGOKU2 SAVE DATA

name: CardDeleteData
note: CARD function 4: delete data (wiki); MAME: card utility DELETE A DATA (test build), then THERE IS NO DATA.

name: CardReadTitle
note: CARD function 5: read data title (wiki); MAME with a card: runs at boot and in the hardware test

name: CardSaveUserName
note: CARD function 6: save user name (wiki); MAME (card utility test build): writes "AAA" at card offset $11 when END is chosen

name: CardLoadUserName
note: CARD function 7: load user name (wiki); MAME: runs when FILE USER'S NAME opens

name: DeductStartCredits
note: after CART_PLAYER_START: for P1 and P2 (DeductPlayerCredit) takes the credits and counts the start in book keeping; MAME: credits 02 -> 01 on START

name: DeductPlayerCredit
note: if the player's bit is set in BIOS_START_FLAG: unless free play (hard DIP 7) subtracts 1 from Credits in BCD (not below 0), then updates the book keeping counters

name: BookKeepingCount
note: adds to a book keeping counter at a2 (called for several counters per start)

name: CardLock
note: locks the memory card (REG_CRDLOCK1/2); pushed as the return address by Card, so it runs after every CARD call

name: ControllerTest
note: unreferenced in SP-S2 (no call, jump or pointer to it): draws CONTROLLER TEST and shows the P1/P2 input bits as 0/1 every frame, never returns; ran in MAME from the hidden-programs build (scenario controller_test)

name: PutInputBits
note: appends 10 characters 0/1 for the low bits of d1 (ControllerTest)

name: ControllerTestText
note: MESS_OUT data of the controller test screen

name: CardUtility
note: unreferenced in SP-S2: MEMORY CARD UTILITY menu, up/down over 6 lines, A jumps through CardUtilityMenuTable

name: CardUtilityMenuTable
note: 6 entries in menu order: format, display data name, copy, delete, file user's name, END (Reset)

name: CardUtilFormat
note: menu item 1. CARD FORMAT; MAME (test build): FORMAT THE CARD screen

name: CardUtilDisplayNames
note: menu item 2. DISPLAY DATA NAME; MAME (test build, blank card): THERE IS NO DATA.

name: CardUtilCopy
note: menu item 3. COPY A DATA: A copies the chosen data (C all of it) into RAM, CHANGE CARD AND PRESS A BUTTON, then saves it on the new card; THERE IS .. ALREADY IN THIS CARD if it holds that data, MEMORY CARD NOT FORMATTED. for a blank card. MAME (test build, cards swapped): card_util_copy, card_util_copy_same_card, card_util_copy_unformatted

name: CardUtilDelete
note: menu item 4. DELETE A DATA: lists the data, asks DO YOU MIND TO DELETE DATA, deletes through CARD function 4; MAME test build

name: CardUtilUserName
note: menu item 5. FILE USER'S NAME: character grid, A types, END saves through CARD function 6; MAME test build

name: CardUtilityMenuText
note: MESS_OUT data of the MEMORY CARD UTILITY menu

name: ClearFixLayer
note: resets the MESS_OUT buffer (BIOS_MESS_POINT = $10FF00) and fills the $500 fix-layer words from VRAM $7000 with $20 (space); kicks the watchdog (REG_DIPSW write) in the loop

name: PutHexByte
note: reads a byte at (a1)+ and appends it at (a0)+ as two hex characters

name: ByteToHex
note: d0 byte -> two ASCII hex digits (high in d0, low in d1)

name: NibbleToHex
note: d1 nibble -> ASCII '0'-'9' / 'A'-'F'

name: PutMenuValueLine
note: appends a MESS_OUT line at VRAM d2, highlighted when d6 equals WorkIndexNew, followed by the BCD value d0 (leading 0 as a space)

name: WaitFrameGetP1
note: WaitFrame, then returns P1 change bits in d0 (repeat bits in the high word); special handling when BIOS_P1STATUS is 3

name: CardUtilPutText
note: queues the MESS_OUT text at a2 followed by dat_C15CE0

name: ReadCardDetect
note: d0 = REG_STATUS_B & $30 (memory card detect bits, 0 = card inserted)

name: DivU32
note: unsigned 32-bit division: d4 / d3 -> quotient in d4, remainder in d0

name: CardUnlock
note: unlocks the memory card (REG_CRDUNLOCK1/2); counterpart of CardLock

name: WriteRtcCtrl
note: writes d1 to REG_RTCCTRL (calendar chip data/clock/strobe lines)

name: BcdToBinary
note: d0 BCD byte (00-99) -> binary through BcdToBinaryTable

name: BcdToBinaryTable
note: 256 bytes: binary value of each BCD byte, 0 for invalid digits

name: RtcSendByte
note: sends the 8 bits of d0 LSB first to the calendar chip through WriteRtcCtrl (data, clock high, clock low)

name: RtcReadByte
note: reads 8 bits from the calendar chip (bit 7 of REG_STATUS_A), LSB first, into d0; runs at every boot in MAME

name: RtcSendByteAlt
note: writes a byte to the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar through $280051 (same protocol as RtcSendByte). MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: RtcReadByteAlt
note: reads a byte from the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar at $220001 (same protocol as RtcReadByte). MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: WriteRtcCtrlAlt
note: writes d1 to $280051, the control of the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: FillVramWords
note: writes d0 to (a0) d1+1 times (REG_VRAMRW with auto-increment)

name: IsSnkRomCard
note: compares the card header with "SNK ROM " (dat_C144F0): detects a read-only SNK ROM card

name: SnkRomCardId
note: "SNK ROM " card header

name: SwitchSlot
note: after sub_C11FB2: slot d5 to CurrentSlot and REG_SLOT, then the cartridge fix layer (REG_CRTFIX) and vectors (REG_SWPROM)

name: WriteLedData
note: writes d5 (inverted) to REG_LEDDATA and pulses REG_LEDLATCHES ($F7 between two $FF), with Delay

name: LockBackupRamUnless
note: locks backup RAM (REG_SRAMLOCK) unless ram_10FEBF is set

name: RtcCommandAlt
note: 4-bit command to the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar, like RtcCommand. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: PutBitChar
note: appends 0 if the Z flag is set on entry, else 1 (I/O check)

name: RtcClockPulse
note: pulses the calendar clock line: WriteRtcCtrl 2 then 0

name: ReadCalendarAlt
note: reads the date and time of the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar into BIOS_YEAR..; called only by CheckCartridgeId. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: SetupCalendarAlt
note: after CheckCalendarDate, writes BIOS_SECOND.. to the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar; called by HwTestCalendar when D is pressed and NeoClnSlot is set ($C17CBE), before SetupCalendar writes the board calendar. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus (D pressed)

name: RtcClockPulseAlt
note: pulses the clock line of the NEO-CLN cartridge calendar: WriteRtcCtrlAlt 2 then 0. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: CheckCalendarDate
note: converts BIOS_YEAR/BIOS_MONTH.. from BCD and checks them against limits (dat_C12FEC); d7 non-zero when invalid; runs before SetupCalendar in MAME

name: CreditCheckPlayer
note: CreditCheck, per player: BCD credits in d0 minus the credits asked in (a0) (BIOS_CREDIT_DEC1, then BIOS_CREDIT_DEC2 by falling through); clears (a0) when there are not enough. In title/demo mode with DEC1 = 0, DEC2 is checked doubled ($C11816). Ran in MAME (game start)

name: CallDeductStartCredits
note: jsr DeductStartCredits; rts (CheckPlayerStart, after a start is accepted and BIOS_SYSTEM_MODE_LO = 3)

name: DemoEndCheck
note: SystemIo while BIOS_USER_MODE = 1 (title/demo): a first coin (credits, no free play) sets system mode 6, SELECT P1 / P2 (BIOS_STATCHANGE_RAW bits 1 / 3) mode 4 / 5; then CART_DEMO_END and SystemReturn. Also sets the LED latches. MAME: the coin path ran (coin_start); the SELECT path did not

name: SystemType
note: system type byte, $80 = MVS (NeoGeoDev wiki System ROM); Reset copies the word $C00400 into BIOS_MVS_FLAG and BIOS_COUNTRY_CODE

name: SystemRegion
note: region byte, 2 = Europe in SP-S2 (0 Japan, 1 USA; NeoGeoDev wiki System ROM); read by the test mode, the card code and GetSoftDipPointer

name: CardStillInserted
note: system mode 3 (back from the game) while a memory card is still inserted (REG_STATUS_B bits 4-5 = 0): maps the system ROM vectors and fix, shows YOUR CARD IS STILL INSERTED. (CardStillInsertedTextJp when BIOS_COUNTRY_CODE = 0), flashes palette entry $400002 for up to 256 frames or until the card is removed, then maps the cartridge back. Ran in MAME after the Sengoku 2 card save

name: CardStillInsertedTextJp
note: Japanese text of CardStillInserted (BIOS_COUNTRY_CODE = 0), MESS_OUT format

name: CardStillInsertedText
note: YOUR CARD IS STILL INSERTED. (MESS_OUT format, BIOS_COUNTRY_CODE not 0)

name: GetSoftDipPointer
note: a0 = the cartridge soft DIP block for this system ROM's region: SystemRegion indexes CART_SOFTDIP_JP / _US / _EU; used by LoadGameSoftDips

name: RtcReadBits
note: bit loop of RtcReadByte, entered with d7 = bits - 1: ReadCalendar reads the last 4 bits (weekday) this way

name: RtcReadBitsAlt
note: bit loop of RtcReadByteAlt, entered with d7 = bits - 1. MAME: ran with a NEO-CLN header (patched Sengoku 2, scenario neo_cln_cartridge); MAME has no chip there, so the values read are open bus

name: CheckCartridgeId
note: slot scan, per slot: Z set (d7 = 0) for a game: CART_NEOGEO_ID = NEO-GEO and the code at CART_SECURITY_PTR (even address) equal to the 122 bytes at $C146A2-$C1471B of the system ROM's card code. CART_NEOGEO_ID = NEO-CLN: a cartridge with its own calendar chip (I: a service cartridge for setting the time): stores the slot in NeoClnSlot, clears the first long of BackupRamSignature, copies the cartridge calendar to the board calendar (ReadCalendarAlt, SetupCalendar) and jumps to HardwareTest, which opens on its calendar screen. NoGoIdText: sets SlotNumberMode, clears the first long of BackupRamSignature and SlotTable, returns Z set (a game). MAME: both special IDs ran (scenarios neo_cln_cartridge, nogo_cartridge)

name: NeoGeoIdText
note: NEO-GEO, compared with CART_NEOGEO_ID by CheckCartridgeId

name: NeoClnIdText
note: NEO-CLN, compared with CART_NEOGEO_ID by CheckCartridgeId: the cartridge calendar path

name: NoGoIdText
note: bytes N 0 O 0 G 0 O 0, compared with CART_NEOGEO_ID by CheckCartridgeId (the even letters of NEO-GEO with 0 between, as a cartridge with one byte lane would read: I). Sets SlotNumberMode. MAME: patched Sengoku 2 (scenario nogo_cartridge) skips the boot animation, shows SLOT 1 for 300 frames, then runs the game

name: BackupRamOkText
note: BACKUP RAM OK ! (16 bytes) compared with BackupRamSignature by BackupRamTest

name: BackupRamDefaults
note: 13 bytes copied to $D0003A-$D00046 by ClearBackupRam (settings defaults; fields not named yet)

name: Card1MIdText
note: NEO-GEO, written one letter per word at +$40 of a 1M memory card when CodeNumberWrite formats it

name: CodeNumberTextJp
note: CODE NUMBER SETTING screen text, Japanese (SystemRegion = 0)

name: CodeNumberSetTextJp
note: Japanese of CodeNumberSetText

name: CardInvalidTextJp
note: Japanese of CardInvalidText

name: CodeNumberSetText
note: CODE NUMBER HAS BEEN SET. (MAME: test_code_number_digits, card1m_format)

name: CardInvalidText
note: THIS CARD IS INVALID. (MAME: test_code_number_blank_card, test_code_number_card)

name: DipSw1OffText
note: DIP-SW 1 OFF !!: TestMenuExit while the Setting Mode DIP is still on (MAME: test_menu_exit)

name: HardDipDraw
note: draws the hard DIP rows from HardDipRows: one digit per bit of the mask (. elsewhere), then the matching value text

name: HardDipRows
note: per row: bit mask word, then (value, text pointer) pairs ended by a negative word; SETTING MODE, COMMUNICATION, FREE PLAY, STOP MODE

name: HardDipOffText
note: OFF (one-bit rows)

name: HardDipOnText
note: ON (one-bit rows)

name: HardDipCommOffText
note: OFF (COMMUNICATION row)

name: HardDipComm1Text
note: ON [No 1] (COMMUNICATION row, cabinet number)

name: HardDipComm2Text
note: ON [No 2]

name: HardDipComm3Text
note: ON [No 3]

name: HardDipComm4Text
note: ON [No 4]

name: HardDipText
note: SETTING UP THE HARD DIP screen text

note: TestCalendar: cursor column to calendar byte

note: after the power-on tests: clears the slot-mode fields, reads the calendar (start of the hour clock), on a new date advances the book keeping day (and month) rings, sets the slot count (bram_D00047: 2, 4 or 6 from REG_SYSTYPE and REG_STATUS_A), checks the Z80, scans the slots and merges the result into SlotTable; on a new day BookNewDayPerGame

name: ScanSlots
note: for each slot: selects it, CheckCartridgeId, stores CART_NGH in the table at $10FD00 (4 bytes per slot) and keeps in bram_D00058 the first slot whose CART_EYECATCH_FLAG is 0

name: SoundSlotSwitch
note: unless the Z80 already replies 1: sends sound command 1 (prepare for a slot switch, NeoGeoDev wiki) and waits up to 8 x 4 VBlanks for the reply 1; called by SwitchSlot and the slot code

name: SlotClearDuplicates
note: unless SlotNumberMode: clears the later slots holding the same NGH as an earlier one (NoGoIdText keeps duplicates, scenario nogo_cartridge)

name: SlotListRemoved
note: lists in bram_D00164 (8 entries of 8 bytes) the games of the stored SlotTable that are no longer in any slot

name: SlotKeepOuterEntries
note: for the stored SlotTable entries past the slot count: their settings go to the same game if it is now in a slot, else to the removed list

name: SlotCopyMovedSettings
note: a game found in another slot than before keeps its settings index (+2) and date (+$20) from the stored SlotTable

name: SlotTableStore
note: writes the scanned slots to SlotTable, then the removed games after them

name: SlotDateNewGames
note: a game with no settings index yet ($FFFF) gets LastBootDate as its date

name: BookNewDayPerGame
note: on a new day: for each slot with a game, advances the game's day index (bram_D0011A, 36-day ring), clears and dates that day's record in BookGameDays and adds 1 to its long at $D00200

name: SaveGameSoftDips
note: copies BIOS_GAME_DIP (16 bytes) back to GameSoftDips for the game in CurrentSlot

name: SaveGameBackupData
note: copies the game's backup area (CART_BACKUP_PTR, CART_BACKUP_SIZE bytes) to backup RAM $D00320 + game index x $1000

name: PreviousSlot
note: selects the previous slot holding a game and loads it (loc_C123F6, as NextSlot); never ran

name: LoadCurrentSlot
note: loads the backup data and soft DIPs of the game in CurrentSlot without switching (loc_C1241E)

name: NextSlot
note: selects the next slot holding a game: slot number on the LEDs, SwitchSlot, sound command 3; then copies the game's backup data from $D00320 + index x $1000, its soft DIPs to BIOS_GAME_DIP and sets the book keeping pointers (bram_D0010A, D001A4, D001A8, D0010E)

name: BookGameMonthsTable
note: BookGameMonths + game index x $C0, 8 entries

name: GetGameDaysPtr
note: a0 = the BookGameDays area of the game in slot bram_D00109 (BookGameDaysTable)

name: BookGameDaysTable
note: BookGameDays + game index x $240, 8 entries

name: GetGameDayCountPtr
note: a0 = $D00200 + game index x 4 (a long incremented by BookNewDayPerGame)

name: GetGameHourCountsPtr
note: a0 = $D0A1A0 + game index x $60 (tbl_C12572): 24 longs, one per hour, incremented by DeductPlayerCredit at index bram_D0005A (the hour clock)

name: BookClearDatedRecord
note: clears the 16-byte record d0 of the ring at a0 and stores LastBootDate in it

name: BookClearRecord
note: clears the 16-byte record at a0 + d0

name: HourClockTick
note: software clock started from the calendar at power-on: every 60 VBlanks (bram_D0005D) adds a second (D0005C), minute (D0005B) and hour x 4 (D0005A, 0-$5C)

name: CountCoin
note: a coin on input d3: counts it (bram_D00024 + d4), adds it to today's and this month's CABINET/COIN records (offset d5), and when enough coins are in (Coin1Coins/Coin2Coins) gives the credits (Coin1Credits/Coin2Credits) to Credits in BCD, at most 99

name: CountService
note: the service switch: adds to the SERVICE counters of today's and this month's records and 1 credit

name: CreditDownCount
note: CREDIT_DOWN: for P1 and P2 with BIOS_CREDIT_DEC1/2 set, takes the credit and counts the play like DeductPlayerCredit (CreditDownPlayer)

name: CreditDownPlayer
note: one player of CreditDownCount (enters DeductPlayerCredit at loc_C1293C)

name: PlayCoinSound
note: once per counted coin (ram_10FEE2), in system mode 2 or more: calls CART_COIN_SOUND, or sends sound command $7F

name: Card1MSaveWords
note: copies d7 words from a1 to the 1M card at a0, writing (a3) each word (Card1MSaveCabinet; Card1MCopyWords is the recover side)

name: BookAddPlayTime
note: adds the counted play time (bram_D00048) to the PLAY TIME field (+$C) of today's, this month's and the game's records, then clears it

name: FixSetPalette1
note: sets palette 1 ($1000) on d7+1 fix-layer words from the current VRAM address (crosshatch border)

name: IoCheckNextSlotLed
note: I/O check: every 64 frames shows the next slot number (1 to the slot count) on the slot LED (IoCheckShowSlot)

name: IoCheckNextLedCount
note: I/O check: every 64 frames adds 11 (BCD) to the LED test count (00, 11 .. 99) and shows it on both LED counters

name: IoCheckPutSystemBits
note: I/O check: REG_SYSTYPE bit 7 and bits 0-2 of bram_D00021 as 0/1

name: IoCheckPutDips
note: I/O check: the 8 hard DIP switches as 0/1

name: IoCheckPutPlayerBits
note: I/O check: 10 bits of one player (joystick byte and two bits of ram_10FEDC) as 0/1

name: IoCheckShowSlot
note: writes WorkIndexNew to the slot LED (WriteLedData) and prints the slot digit

name: IoCheckShowLed1
note: the LED test count on the first LED counter (latch $EF) and on screen

name: IoCheckShowLed2
note: the LED test count on the second LED counter (latch $DF, digit order reversed) and on screen

name: SoundTestCommands
note: sound commands of the 4 sound test items ($03, $5D, $5C, $5E)

name: SoundTestMoveCursor
note: sound test: erases the cursor at the old item and draws it at ram_10FCDF

name: SoundTestPutCursor
note: MESS_OUT entry for the sound test cursor

name: SoundTestDrawItems
note: sound test: draws the item lines, the playing one (ram_10FCE2) in another text

name: HwCalendarShowDate
note: hardware-test calendar: prints month, day, year, hour, minute, second (PutMenuValueLine)

name: EyecatchFadeStep
note: next step of the eyecatcher colour fade: colour set from EyecatchFadeIndex[WorkIndexNew] (EyecatchSetColours)

name: EyecatchSetSprites
note: writes 18 sprite columns from VRAM address d0 (step $40): 4 tiles from a0 with attribute d1, then 28 empty tiles

name: EyecatchSetColours
note: queues colour set d0 (12 bytes at EyecatchColourSets) for the next VBlank: 5 colours to $4001E2 and the backdrop $401FFE

name: EyecatchFadeIndex
note: colour set number for each step of the eyecatcher fade

name: EyecatchColourSets
note: 12-byte colour sets (5 colours and the backdrop) of the eyecatcher fade

name: DelayLonger
note: nested BSR chain (DelayLonger > Delay > DelayShort > DelayShorter > DelayReturn): the depth sets the delay; used around Z80 and LED writes

name: DelayShort
note: see DelayLonger

name: DelayShorter
note: see DelayLonger

name: DelayReturn
note: the rts that ends the delay chain

name: CopyControllerState
note: copies a player's status block (BIOS_P1STATUS..) to ram_10FEE8/ram_10FEEE; a mahjong controller (status 3, wiki) is converted to joystick bits first

name: MahjongKeysToJoystick
note: maps a mahjong controller key byte to joystick bits (bit 7 from bit 0 of d1, nibbles swapped)

name: MahjongStartFilter
note: mahjong controller: drops START/SELECT bit d0 while one of the keys in the mask is held

name: UpdatePlayerInputs
note: updates a player's input block (and the expanded block at +$C), or the mahjong rows

name: UpdateInputBlock
note: previous, current, change and repeat bytes of one input block; repeat after 16 frames, then every 8

name: UpdateMahjongRow
note: current and change bytes of one mahjong key row

name: ReadMahjongRows
note: reads two more key rows through REG_POUTPUT ($24 and $09) into d6

name: MessOutCommands
note: MESS_OUT command handlers 0-13: end, format, auto-increment, VRAM address, data at a pointer, add to address, resume data, inline data, 8x16 tiles, 8x16 text, call a list, return, repeat a word, write increasing words

name: MessOutEnd
note: MESS_OUT command 0: end of the list (next list pointer)

name: MessOutFormat
note: MESS_OUT command 1: data format in d5 (bytes or words, end code or count)

name: MessOutIncrement
note: MESS_OUT command 2: VRAM auto-increment

name: MessOutAddress
note: MESS_OUT command 3: VRAM address

name: MessOutDataPointer
note: MESS_OUT command 4: writes the data at a pointer (MessOutData)

name: MessOutAddAddress
note: MESS_OUT command 5: adds to the VRAM address

name: MessOutData
note: MESS_OUT command 6 and the data writer: bytes or words from a2 to VRAM, until the end code or for a count (format bits 16-17 of d5)

name: MessOutDataInline
note: MESS_OUT command 7: data that follows the command, then aligns the list pointer

name: MessOutTiles8x16
note: MESS_OUT command 8: a row of 8x16 characters given as tile numbers, upper then lower half

name: MessOutText8x16
note: MESS_OUT command 9: a row of 8x16 ASCII text, upper then lower half (MessOutText8x16Row)

name: MessOutText8x16Row
note: one half-row of MessOutText8x16: maps each character to its tile until $FF

name: MessOutTiles8x16Row
note: one half-row of MessOutTiles8x16: writes the bytes as tile numbers until $FF

name: MessOutCall
note: MESS_OUT command 10: runs another list (pointer pushed at ram_10FEC6)

name: MessOutReturn
note: MESS_OUT command 11: back from MessOutCall

name: MessOutRepeat
note: MESS_OUT command 12: writes one word d1 times

name: MessOutSequence
note: MESS_OUT command 13: writes d1 words, adding 1 each time

name: HwCalendarFixAddresses
note: 6 fix-layer addresses ($7157, $71D7, $7257, $715A, $71DA, $725A) after HwTestCalendar; nothing refers to them (leftover)

name: CardFillTest
note: unreferenced (no call, jump or pointer; it was typed as data until 2026-11-15): saves $40 bytes from $100000 with CARD 3 again and again, NGH $1234 and file numbers 0-15 (counter at $108000), then the next NGH, until a CARD error, which goes to CardError and stops there (jmp to itself): a development test that fills the memory card. Ran in MAME from a test build (scenarios card_full_*): a formatted 2 KB card is full after 27 saves, in one frame, and the full-card list appears

name: CardFillTestTitle
note: 20-byte data title copied to $100000 by CardFillTest: tile codes shown as Japanese kana in the full-card list (not ASCII); CardFillTest changes its last byte for each save

name: SystemRomChecksum
note: checksum byte of the system ROM (NeoGeoDev wiki, SP-E: $4D here; the byte after it is the same); compared by the power-on test

name: SystemIdText
note: NEO-GEO SYSTEM PROGRAM VERSION 0 COPYRIGHT BY SNK CORPORATION (ID text, wiki); its bytes start the checksummed area

name: CardFormatVersion
note: word $0000 just before Reset: CardFormat writes it into the card header (8-bit and 16-bit cards)

name: CardFormatVersionLo
note: low byte of CardFormatVersion (CardFormat for a type $80 card)

name: SystemReturnModes
note: SystemReturn: one handler per system mode (BIOS_SYSTEM_MODE low byte 0-6)

name: SystemIoBuildFlag
note: word $0001 tested by SystemIo, whose branch goes to the next instruction either way: a leftover build switch

name: StartCreditsNeeded
note: credits needed for the start bits 1-3 (P1, P2, both): 1, 1, 2 (StartCreditCheck)

name: StartFlagResult
note: BIOS_START_FLAG for the start bits with enough credits (first 4) or not (last 4: 0)

name: BookGameHoursTable
note: $D0A1A0 + game index x $60, 8 entries (GetGameHourCountsPtr)

name: YearWeekdayTable
note: 100 bytes: weekday offset of each year 00-99 (CheckCalendarDate computes the weekday from it)

name: MonthDaysTable
note: days per month: 29 (February of a leap year), then January-December 31, 28, 31, 30 ..

name: MonitorVramSteps
note: debug monitor DISPLAY V-RAM: value added for each address digit

name: MonitorMemorySteps
note: MODIFY MEMORY: value added for each digit (6 address digits, then the value digits)

name: MonitorVramDigitMoves
note: MODIFY V-RAM: next digit for Left/Right

name: MonitorModifyVramSteps
note: MODIFY V-RAM: value added for each digit

name: MonitorRegisterDigitMoves
note: MODIFY REGISTER: next digit for Left/Right

name: MonitorRegisterSteps
note: MODIFY REGISTER: value added for each value digit

name: MonitorRegisterNames
note: register names D0-D7, A0-A7, SR, PC (4 bytes each, MESS_OUT text)

name: MonitorBlankRow
note: 19 tile codes $FF ended by 0: the rows of MonitorCommandLine

name: ScreenVersionTile
note: tile $35 (5) written at fix address $7484 (top right) on the test menu and the hardware-test colour bars; the 5 seen in the MAME screenshots

name: IoCheckText
note: MESS_OUT data of the I/O CHECK screen

name: SoundTestItemTexts
note: for each of the 4 sound test items, the text while playing and the normal text

name: SoundTestOffText
note: SOUND OFF

name: SoundTestRightTextLit

name: SoundTestRightText
note: RIGHT

name: SoundTestLeftTextLit
note: LEFT while playing (sound command $5C)

name: SoundTestLeftText
note: LEFT

name: SoundTestCenterTextLit
note: CENTER while playing (sound command $5E)

name: SoundTestCenterText
note: CENTER

name: SoundTestText
note: MESS_OUT data of the SOUND TEST screen

name: MemCardTestText
note: MESS_OUT data of the MEMORY CARD TEST screen

name: MemCardTestOkText
note: MEMORY CARD TEST OK

name: MemCardTestErrorText
note: MEMORY CARD TEST ERROR

name: BackupClearText
note: MESS_OUT data of the BACKUP CLEAR screen

name: HwCalendarFieldOrder
note: hardware-test calendar: the field shown on each line (month, day, year, hour, minute, second)

note: largest BCD value of each calendar field (12, 31, 23, 59, 59)

note: MESS_OUT data of SETTING UP THE CALENDAR (hardware test)

note: 10 step routines of the eyecatcher, by WorkIndex

name: EyecatchSpriteInit
note: MESS_OUT list sent first by Eyecatcher (writes sprite control data at VRAM $8400 and $8200)

note: for each of the 4 buttons, the MESS_OUT data released and pressed

note: fix words ($F0xx: palette F, tile xx) drawn one by one by an eyecatcher step (pointer in ram_10FCE2)
